distance_note: The dry docks belong to the Pier 68/70 shipyard, next to Crane Cove Park and outside the tracked Pier 70 boundary (the Port's December 2025 park release describes new fencing along the Shipyard at the park's east side). Sources differ on when the shipyard closed: the Port's January and February 2026 memos say it operated until 2016 and has been inactive since, while a Port slide and Potrero View say 2017.
summary: Two Port-owned floating dry docks at Piers 68 & 70 -- Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock -- that the Port Commission's President and the Port's Executive Director declared an emergency over on 2025-12-08 after hull tears and uncontrolled ballast-tank flooding caused Dry Dock No. 2 to list. The Port is carrying out emergency stabilization repairs to Dry Dock No. 2 and plans to demolish and dispose of both structures; no source reports that demolition has begun. The total estimated cost is $61.2M; as of February 2026 about $20.0M was identified ($18.5M of a requested supplemental appropriation plus $1.5M of BAE settlement funds) and the remaining $41.2M was anticipated in the FY2026-27 budget.

milestones.text: Port Commission authorizes Resolution 24-51 funding toward Pier 70 shipyard dry dock work; the formal supplemental appropriation ordinance was introduced later (see 2025-12 and 2026-02 entries).

Existing tears in Dry Dock No. 2's hull enlarge and new tears appear, causing uncontrolled flooding of ballast tanks; the dry dock is then found to have excessive listing on its northeast side following a rainstorm.
The Port Commission President and Executive Director declare the existence of an emergency over Dry Dock No. 2's condition.
Mayor introduces a supplemental appropriation ordinance for dry dock emergency stabilization and future demolition funding.

Port Commission takes up Calendar Item 9A, an informational item with no action required, on the dry dock emergency. The staff memo for it is dated 2026-01-09 and says: auxiliary industrial pumps installed by Port Maintenance staff to pump out the ballast tanks, with staff moving portable pumps from tank to tank; emergency repairs (welding and patching to reduce water intake, and stabilizing or removing the cranes on the wing walls) at a total not-to-exceed cost of $10,000,000; proposals received from three marine contractors on 2026-01-05, with the contract award anticipated the week of 2026-01-20 (so not yet awarded when the memo was written); and staff's anticipation of advertising a demolition-services contract in summer 2026. The 2026-01-13 meeting date is from the Capital Planning Committee's timeline; the memo itself carries only its own date.

Capital Planning Committee item: the Port asks the committee to consider and approve a $18.5M supplemental appropriation, in a memo dated 2026-02-09 whose cost table shows $61.2M total estimated cost to stabilize and dispose of Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock. About $20.0M of that is the $18.5M requested appropriation plus $1.5M of existing BAE settlement funds; the other $41.2M is an anticipated FY2026-27 appropriation ("anticipated additional appropriation of funds in the FY 2026-27 capital budget"). No source read reports the committee's decision or whether either appropriation was adopted.

Expected, as announced by the Port in January 2026, and since superseded: Port staff anticipate advertising a contract for demolition services in the summer of 2026 (memo dated 2026-01-09: "Port staff anticipates advertising a contract for demolition services in the summer of 2026"). The Port's Feb 9, 2026 presentation to the Capital Planning Committee instead lists "Spring 2026: Award of final demolition and construction contract". An expected date; no source read reports that either happened, and the later reports (see the 2026-07 entry) put the tender in the second half of 2027. Dated to the end of summer 2026.

Potrero View reports the Port has directed an outside engineering firm to prepare preliminary engineering plans for demolition of both dry docks and help secure permits; a Port spokesperson is quoted saying the package will be used "to advertise for a future design-build contract". Separately, in its own words rather than as a quotation, Potrero View says the Port expects initial plans to be completed by March 2027 and a demolition contract tendered in the second half of 2027 (the Port, as reported by Potrero View). This is later than the summer 2026 advertising the January 2026 Port memo anticipated.

Expected: demolition contract to be tendered in the second half of 2027, and initial plans completed by March 2027 (the Port, as reported by Potrero View on 2026-07-15, in the article's own wording rather than a quotation). SFist (2026-03-05) similarly reports, citing KPIX, that "the Port is now saying it will be 2027 before they can get a contractor to come in and start the demolition". These are expected dates reported by the press, not Port-published dates; demolition has not begun.

costs.what: Not-to-exceed cost of the emergency repairs (welding and patching to reduce water intake, and stabilizing or removing the cranes on the Dry Dock No. 2 wing walls) under the Port's December 2025 emergency declaration, as stated in the memo dated 2026-01-09; the Port's Feb 9, 2026 memo to the Capital Planning Committee budgets the emergency work at $10,477,828 including a 20% contingency and a $200,000 reserve (Table 1), which is above this ceiling

Total estimated cost to stabilize and dispose of Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock (Phase 1A stabilization $8.6M + Dry Dock No. 2 disposal $27.4M + Eureka disposal $15.7M + $9.5M contingency, per the Port's Feb 9, 2026 cost table to the Capital Planning Committee; the Port's Jan 9, 2026 memo splits the same $61.2M differently, with Phase 1A at $7.2M and a $10.0M contingency); about $20.0M was identified as of Feb 2026 ($18.5M requested supplemental appropriation plus $1.5M of BAE settlement funds) and roughly $41.2M was anticipated in the FY2026-27 budget; no source read reports that either was adopted

open_questions: The Eureka Dry Dock's length is given as 528 feet by Mission Local (2026-02-23) and as 570 feet by Potrero View (2026-07-15) and by a slide in the Port's Feb 9, 2026 presentation to the Capital Planning Committee ("Eureka (570' x 125')"); the Port's January 2026 memo gives no length for it, and the sources conflict, so no length is shown as settled here. Both sources give 1945 as its build year and 900 feet and 1970 for Dry Dock No. 2.

Whether the Board of Supervisors adopted the $18.5M supplemental appropriation (ordinance File 251248, introduced Dec 16, 2025) and whether the remaining $41.2M was appropriated in the FY2026-27 budget is not reported in any source read; the Port's Feb 9, 2026 memo shows the $18.5M and $1.5M of BAE settlement funds as the first $20.0M of the $61.2M total.

Whether demolition will be completed "before winter storms" (a claim in an unsourced summary, not repeated in this record) is not supported by any primary source found; SFist (2026-03-05) reports it will likely be a year before the dry dock situation is resolved, and roughly $41.2M of the $61.2M total remained unfunded as of Feb 2026.

Has demolition of the dry docks begun, or has the Port advertised or awarded a demolition contract? As of 2026-10-12 no source read reports that demolition began, and no Port Commission item or Port contract notice was found reporting an advertisement or award; the July 2026 Potrero View report describes the design-build contract as still to come. The dry docks are therefore shown as existing, with demolition planned.
What becomes of BAE Systems' ship-repair operations at the adjacent Pier 70 shipyard once these dry docks are removed is not addressed in the sources reviewed here.
